Description: This course is designed to prepare students to be effective teachers of emergent bilingual (EB) students, value their bilingualism and biculturalism, and apply an asset-based approach to educating students whose first language is not English. Not for credit towards the bilingual or ESL endorsements. Should not be taken in addition to TCH 419, TCH 420, and/or TCH 424.  Prerequisites: TCH 498a03 with concurrent enrollment.
This course will provide students with a foundation in the history, policies, theory, research, and practice of bilingual/bicultural education.

This course focuses on the assessment of bilingual learners. This course counts as the bilingual education assessment course for the State of Illinois requirements for bilingual approval and endorsement  Prerequisite: TCH 419; Not for credit if earned credit in TCH 320.

Study of the classical functions of early adolescent education and the relationship of these functions to contemporary institutional/instructional settings. This course includes 20 clinical hours. Prerequisites: A national criminal background check will be required for the clinical portion of this course.

Course Title: Developmental Issues In Early Adolescent Education
Description: Examination of developmental patterns and issues in the education of early adolescents in middle level schools. This course includes 20 clinical hours. Prerequisites: National Criminal Background Check will be required for the clinical portion of this course.

Course Title: Methods and Materials for Bilingual and English Learners
Description: This course focuses on the methods and materials used to meet the needs of individual English learners.
This course will offer knowledge of biliteracy development for teachers to support culturally and linguistically diverse K-12 learners. Prerequisite: TCH 419 or SED 408

Applications of theories of learning and models of instructional design to methods of instruction through a design process. Formerly Educational Technology in the Content Areas and Instructional Technology in Educational Settings. Prerequisite: TCH 401.

Focuses on uses of technologies across academic disciplines, and the development of instruction that integrates accessible technologies aligned to content and technology standards. Prerequisites: TCH 401

Middle level curriculum focuses on curriculum designs, principles of curriculum development, theoretical foundations, and problems encountered by practitioners in middle level education. Course requires 20 clinical hours. Prerequisites: TCH 421 and TCH 423 required. National Criminal Background Check required.
This course focuses on the authentic assessment of the reading process. Prerequisites: TCH 498a03  with concurrent enrollment.

Examines the historical and practical issues of distance teaching and learning, along with current system-wide capacities of support for online, hybrid, and blended instruction and connected learning in educational settings. Provides an opportunity to develop and evaluate curricula and technology plans in educational settings. Prerequisites: TCH 401

Course Title: Foundations and Management Of School Libraries
Description: Explores the roles of the school librarian in administration and leadership of school libraries including planning for integration into the curriculum, supervision, assessment, budgeting, collection development, collaboration with administration and teachers.
This course will provide students with an understanding of two-way family engagement and how to collaborate with families and communities through equitable approaches.

Course Title: Organization & Access To Information In The School Library
Description: Organizing and making information accessible through classification, technology, knowledge of legal and professional guidelines, facilities planning, and policy information.
Advanced graduate study of curricular and instructional topics. Multiple enrollments allowed if topic different for maximum of 9 hours.
Provision of assistance in finding, evaluating, and using information, with emphasis on the knowledge and use of print and online reference sources.

Course Title: Information Literacy Instruction and Reference Services for School Libraries
Description: Integration of school libraries into the curriculum with librarians as teachers, advocates, and collaborators in providing reference support and implementing information literacy instruction.

This course will provide students with an understanding of equitable instructional methods and inclusive pedagogies used to teach preservice early childhood teachers.

Course Title: Selection & Use Of Materials In Elementary School Library
Description: Collection development of print and nonprint materials, grades K-8. Emphasis on age-appropriate materials supporting school curriculum and student learning.
An historical review of science education curricula and analysis of contemporary standards-based curricula.
Review and critical analysis of research in science education. Application of research for reflection and improvement of practices in science education.

Course Title: Writing Instruction In The PreK-12 Classroom
Description: Theory and practice combine to engage teachers as writers. Candidates will read, write, and discuss their own writing and the writing of others, and apply this process to classroom practices.
Analysis and application of current theory and research to the design and delivery of science instructional strategies.

Course Title: Selection & Use Of Materials In Secondary School Library
Description: Collection development of print and nonprint materials, grades 6-12. Emphasis on age-appropriate materials supporting school curriculum and student learning.

Explores writing development within historical, social, political, and cultural contexts, and places anti-racism, equity, and inclusion at the heart of this exploration. The aim is to empower educators with nuanced understandings of writing development, equipping them to apply and share these understandings within their unique educational settings.
An overview of the history, research, and practice of literacy coaching in preK-12 schools.

Course Title: Science Methods for Elementary Teaching and Learning
Description: This course focuses on the methods associated with effective elementary science instruction. Emphasis is placed upon activity-based strategies. Prerequisites: TCH 498a05 with concurrent enrollment.

This course focuses on theories, and methods for social studies instruction for elementary education. Students will develop competencies in current directions regarding research, critical perspectives on diversity and inclusion, developmentally appropriate and culturally responsive content, and asset-based approaches centered in geography and history. Prerequisites: TCH 498a05 with concurrent enrollment.

Course Title: Literacy Learning In A Digital World
Description: Study of recent research in literacy learning, emphasizing technology and digital literacies for the improvement of literacy instruction.
Examination of theoretical models and frameworks for literacy and relationships between theory, research, and classroom practice in PK-12 classrooms.

Course Title: Classroom Based Literacy Assessment and Instruction
Description: Evaluation of literacy learning using authentic assessments, standardized tests, observations and portfolios. Field experiences required. It is recommended that TCH 462 be completed prior to enrolling in this course.

Course Title: Critical Interpretation and Application of Literacy Research
Description: This course supports candidates in their development as critical consumers and producers of research, policy, and practice. By focusing on the critical interpretation and application of literacy research, students will advocate for evidence-informed, inclusive and affirming classroom and school literacy learning practices, policies, and environments.

Description: This interdisciplinary course uses an intersectional feminist framework to engage in contemporary conversations about gender, race, sex, sexuality, class, and power in primarily US contexts. Students apply theories learned to both their lived experiences and current events while connecting historical and contemporary issues of social (in)justice.

Students will leave the course with a deeper understanding of queer theatre and the tools needed to meaningfully engage with queer theatre as an audience member or practitioner.

Description: Supervised examination of issues related to the Undergraduate Teaching Experience. Seminar requires time beyond the UTA work experience. A student must have received a B or higher in the assigned course and have at least 6 hours earned in WGS courses. Consent of instructor and program required to enroll. Maximum of 3 hours may be applied toward graduation.

Interdisciplinary survey of lesbian, gay, bisexual, transgender, queer, intersex, and asexual histories, politics, and cultures. Examines struggles for LGBTQIA+ rights as they intersect with social-justice issues pertaining to race, class, citizenship, age, and ability. Topics include identities and subcultures before-and-after medical models of sexuality and gender, liberation movements, AIDS activism, nature-nurture interplay, and queer art, literature, and popular culture.

Course Title: Independent Honor Study In Women's, Gender, And Sexuality Studies
Description: An Honors student investigates a topic of interest within their discipline under the guidance of a faculty member. Multiple enrollments allowed; maximum of 6 hours may be applied toward graduation. Limit of 9 hours HON 299 and 395 may be combined to count toward graduation.

An interdisciplinary approach to the theories and conceptual tools feminist scholars use to address social justice issues across a broad range of topics and academic disciplines. The course explores the historical and contemporary developments in feminist theory with particular attention to how gender intersects with race, ethnicity, class, sexuality, coloniality, and other social identities. Prerequisite: WGS 120

Course Attributes: CRSS - CROSSLIST (1 crse offered by 2+ subjects), IDEA - IDEAS (IDEAS Graduation Requirement)
Description: This class explores the Chicana/Latina/x feminist movements. It examines the historical conditions, current issues, and tensions within the Chicana/Latina/x feminisms through an examination of the foundational writings of Chicana/Latina/x authors. Equivalent course, offered as LAL, SOC, WGS 368; repeat policy will apply. Prerequisite: SOC/LAL 109 or WGS 120.

Interdisciplinary survey of major figures, concepts, and schools of thought informing dialogues and dissonances between feminist, queer, and trans theory. Explores queerness as a category of radical difference that gives LGBTQIA+ cultures their social distinctiveness and political urgency. Deconstructs sex/gender/sexuality at intersections of difference. Considers transnational and queer-people-of-color critiques; defamiliarizes understandings of the body; and offers queer cultural criticism. Prerequisites: WGS 292
